title: A sandstone palace of art built for an exhibition
episode: Glasgow, Scotland: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide
description: Travel writer Rick Steves visits Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, the red sandstone building opened for Glasgow’s 1901 International Exhibition, where free admission puts Salvador Dalí’s Christ of St John of the Cross near a hanging Spitfire.

title: The pedestrian spine of the Victorian city centre
episode: Glasgow, Scotland: Buchanan Street - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide - Travel Bite
description: Rick Steves walks Buchanan Street, Glasgow’s pedestrianised main shopping street, which runs downhill from the Royal Concert Hall to Argyle Street between Victorian sandstone frontages, glass-roofed arcades and street musicians.

title: Gable-end murals across the city centre
episode: Glasgow, Scotland: Graffiti Street Art - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide - Travel Bite
description: Rick Steves on the giant murals painted on Glasgow’s city-centre gable walls, a trail whose best-known stop is the artist Smug’s modern St Mungo, the city’s patron saint, cradling a robin on High Street.
